title: American Declaration of the Rights and Duties of Man

pages.text:
ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COUNCIL / CONSEIL ECONOMIQUE ET SOCIAL

E/CN.4/122/Rev.1*
8 October 1948
FRENCH
ORIGINAL: SPANISH

Dual Distribution

AMERICAN DECLARATION OF THE RIGHTS
AND DUTIES OF MAN

The Ninth International American Conference,

CONSIDERING:

That the American peoples have raised the human person to the status of dignity and that it is recognized in their national constitutions that the juridical and political institutions which govern life in society have as their principal aim the protection of the essential rights of man and the creation of conditions permitting his spiritual and material progress and the attainment of his happiness;

That on several occasions the American States have recognized that the essential rights of man do not have their origin in the fact that he is a national of a given State, but rest above all on the attributes of the human person;

That the international protection of the rights of man must serve as the principal guide to American law in its evolution;

That the American consecration of the essential rights of man, combined with the guarantees offered by the internal regime of the States, constitutes the initial system of protection considered by the American States as suited to present juridical and social conditions, bearing in mind the need to strengthen it ever further in the international field as circumstances become more propitious,

DECIDES:

To adopt the following

AMERICAN DECLARATION OF THE RIGHTS
AND DUTIES OF MAN

PREAMBLE

All men are born free and equal in dignity and rights, and as they are endowed by nature with reason and conscience, they must conduct themselves fraternally towards one another.

The fulfilment of the duty of each is a prerequisite to the right of all. Rights and duties complement each other correlatively

[Footnote: * Official translation made at Bogota.]

French
Page 2

in all the social and political activities of man. If rights exalt individual liberty, duties express the dignity of that liberty.

Duties of a juridical nature presuppose others, of a moral nature, whose conception and foundations are identical.

Since spiritual life is the supreme end of humanity and its highest category, man has the duty to serve the spirit with all his strength and all his resources.

Since culture, from the social and historical point of view, is the highest manifestation of the spirit, man has the duty to cultivate himself, and to sustain and encourage culture, by all the means at his disposal.

Finally, since morality and good conduct constitute the noblest fruits of culture, man has the duty always to venerate them.

CHAPTER ONE
RIGHTS

ARTICLE I. Every human being has the right to life, liberty, security and the integrity of his person.
    [Margin: Right to life, liberty, security and the integrity of the person.]

ARTICLE II. All persons, without distinction of race, sex, language, religion or other, are equal before the law and have the rights and duties consecrated in this declaration.
    [Margin: Right to equality before the law.]

ARTICLE III. Every person has the right freely to profess a religious belief, to manifest it and to practise it in public or in private.
    [Margin: Right to freedom of religion and worship.]

ARTICLE IV. Every person has the right to freedom of investigation, of opinion, of expression and of dissemination of thought by any means whatsoever.
    [Margin: Right to freedom of investigation, opinion, expression and dissemination.]

ARTICLE V. Every person has the right to the protection of the law against abusive attacks upon his honour, his reputation and his private and family life.
    [Margin: Right to the protection of honour, personal reputation and private and family life.]

E/CN.4/122/Rev.1
French
Page 3

ARTICLE VI. Every person has the right to found a family, the fundamental element of society, and to receive protection therefor.
    [Margin: Right to found a family and right to the protection of the family.]

ARTICLE VII. Every pregnant or nursing woman and every child have the right to protection, care and special aid.
    [Margin: Right to the protection of motherhood and childhood.]

ARTICLE VIII. Every person has the right to fix his residence within the territory of the State of which he is a national, to move about freely within it and not to leave it except of his own will.
    [Margin: Rights of residence and movement.]

ARTICLE IX. Every person has the right to the inviolability of his home.
    [Margin: Right to the inviolability of the home.]

ARTICLE X. Every person has the right to the inviolability and free circulation of his correspondence.
    [Margin: Right to the inviolability and free circulation of correspondence.]

ARTICLE XI. Every person has the right to have his health preserved by sanitary and social measures relating to food, clothing, housing and medical care, which shall be established in proportion to public resources and to those of the community.
    [Margin: Right to the preservation of health and to well-being.]

ARTICLE XII. Every person has the right to education, which must be based on the principles of liberty, morality and human solidarity.

Likewise, he has the right to be prepared, by means of this education, for a dignified existence and to be enabled to improve his standard of living and his usefulness to society.
    [Margin: Right to education.]

Page 4

The right to education includes that of equality of opportunity in every case, in accordance with natural gifts, merits and the desire of the individual to profit from the advantages offered to him by the community and the State.

Every person has the right to receive, free of charge and at the least, primary instruction.

ARTICLE XIII. Every person has the right to take part in the cultural life of the community, to enjoy the arts and to benefit from the results of intellectual progress and in particular from scientific discoveries.

Likewise he has the right to the protection of the moral and material interests deriving from inventions or from literary, scientific or artistic works of which he is the author.
    [Margin: Right to the benefits of culture.]

ARTICLE XIV. Every person has the right to work under dignified conditions and to follow his vocation freely, where conditions of employment permit.

Every person who works has the right to receive remuneration commensurate with his capacity or skill and assuring him a suitable standard of living, for himself and for his family.
    [Margin: Right to work and to fair remuneration.]

ARTICLE XV. Every person has the right to rest and to honest leisure, and must have the opportunity to employ his free time usefully for the benefit of his spiritual, cultural and physical improvement.
    [Margin: Right to rest and to the use of leisure hours.]

[illegible]
Page 5

ARTICLE XVI. Every person has the right to social insurance which protects him against the consequences of unemployment, old age and incapacity resulting from any cause whatsoever independent of his will, rendering him physically or mentally incapable of providing for his means of subsistence.
    [Margin: Right to social insurance.]

ARTICLE XVII. Every person has the right to be recognized everywhere as a subject of rights and obligations and to enjoy fundamental civil rights.
    [Margin: Right to the recognition of juridical personality and of civil rights.]

ARTICLE XVIII. Every person may have recourse to the courts to assert his rights. Likewise, there must exist a simple and speedy procedure enabling justice to protect him against acts of authority violating, to his prejudice, certain fundamental rights recognized by the constitution.
    [Margin: Right to justice.]

ARTICLE XIX. Every person has the right to the nationality which legally belongs to him and to change it, if he so desires, for that of any other country willing to grant it to him.
    [Margin: Right to nationality.]

ARTICLE XX. Every person having civil capacity has the right to participate in the government of his country, directly or through his representatives, and to take part in honest, periodic and free popular elections held by secret ballot.
    [Margin: Right of suffrage and of participation in government.]

ARTICLE XXI. Every person has the right to join peaceably, in public meeting or in temporary assembly, with other persons having the same interests, of whatever nature they may be.
    [Margin: Right of assembly.]

E/CN.4/122/Rev.1
French
Page 6

ARTICLE XXII. Every person has the right to associate with others in order to promote and protect his legitimate interests, of a political, economic, religious, social, cultural, professional, trade-union or other nature.
    [Margin: Right of association.]

ARTICLE XXIII. Every person has the right to private property in order to meet the essential needs of a decent life, which contributes to maintaining his dignity and that of his home.
    [Margin: Right to property.]

ARTICLE XXIV. Every person has the right to submit respectful petitions to any competent authority, for reasons of general interest or of private interest, and to obtain a prompt decision.
    [Margin: Right of petition.]

ARTICLE XXV. No one may be deprived of his liberty except in the cases and according to the forms established by existing laws.

No one may be imprisoned for failure to fulfil obligations of an exclusively civil character.

Every individual who has been deprived of his liberty has the right to have the judge verify immediately the legality of that measure and to be tried without delay or, otherwise, to be released. He also has the right to humane treatment during his detention.
    [Margin: Right to protection against arbitrary detention.]

ARTICLE XXVI. Every accused person is considered innocent until such time as his guilt is proved.

Every person accused of an offence has the right to be given a hearing in
    [Margin: Right to due process of law.]

French
Page 7

an impartial and public hearing, to be tried by courts previously established under already existing laws, and not to be sentenced to cruel, degrading or unusual punishment.

ARTICLE XXVII. Every person has the right to seek and receive asylum in foreign territory, in case of persecution not motivated by ordinary-law offences, and in accordance with the legislation of each country and with international agreements.
    [Margin: Right of asylum.]

ARTICLE XXVIII. The rights of each man are limited by the rights of others, by the security of all and by the just demands of the general welfare and of the development of democracy.
    [Margin: Scope of the rights of man.]

CHAPTER TWO
DUTIES

ARTICLE XXIX. Every person has the duty to maintain with his fellow men relations enabling each, as well as all, to form and develop his personality fully.
    [Margin: Duties towards society.]

ARTICLE XXX. Every person has the duty to aid, support, educate and protect his minor children, and children have the duty to respect their parents at all times and to aid, support and protect them in case of need.
    [Margin: Duties of children and parents.]

ARTICLE XXXI. Every person has the duty to acquire, at the least, primary instruction.
    [Margin: Duty to acquire an education.]

French
Page 8

ARTICLE XXXII. Every person has the duty to vote in the popular elections of the country of which he is a national, when he has civil capacity to do so.
    [Margin: Duty of suffrage.]

ARTICLE XXXIII. Every person has the duty to submit to the law and to the other legitimate provisions of the authorities of the country in which he is.
    [Margin: Duty of obedience to the law.]

ARTICLE XXXIV. Every person fit for service has the duty to render the civil and military services which the Fatherland may require for its defence and preservation and, in case of public calamity, to render the services of which he is capable.

He likewise has the duty to fulfil the offices of popular election which fall to him in the State of which he is a national.
    [Margin: Duty to serve the community and the nation.]

ARTICLE XXXV. Every person is obliged to co-operate with the State and the community in mutual aid and social security, according to his means and the circumstances.
    [Margin: Duties of mutual aid and social security.]

ARTICLE XXXVI. Every person has the duty to pay the taxes fixed by law for the support of the public services of his country.

ARTICLE XXXVII. Every person has the duty to work, to the extent of his capacities and possibilities, in order to obtain the resources necessary for his subsistence or for the benefit of the community.
    [Margin: Duty to work.]

ARTICLE XXXVIII. Every person has the duty to refrain from taking part in political activities which, according to the law, are reserved to the citizens of the State in which he resides as an alien.
    [Margin: Duty to refrain from political activities in a foreign country.]

uncertain.french: Si les droits exaltent la liberté individuelle
uncertain.issue: The verb is faint on the scan; the letter shapes (seven letters, an ascender in fourth position, no 'p' descender) fit 'exaltent' rather than 'expriment', so 'exalt' is used, but the word is not fully legible.

issues.french: Si les droits ex[a]ltent la liberté individuelle, les devoirs expriment la dignité de cette liberté.
issues.translation: If rights express individual liberty, duties express the dignity of that liberty.
issues.suggestion: If rights exalt individual liberty, duties express the dignity of that liberty. The verb is faint on the scan, but its shape (ex..l.ent, with an 'l', and typed differently from the 'expriment' that follows) points to 'exaltent'. The translation repeats 'express' and loses the contrast between the two verbs.
